title: ReconFormer: Accelerated MRI Reconstruction Using Recurrent Transformer
grouping: Three lettered panels without frames: (a) fills the top band, (b) and (c) share the bottom row. In (a) three scale heads are stacked vertically, rows labelled 'Scale Head 1-3', columns headed Query, Key, Value, each head's query-key pair closed by thin square brackets. One colour per head (green, orange, blue) groups everything that belongs to that scale.
shapes_depth: (a) starts from an MRI slice thumbnail with a white patch grid and translucent coloured squares of three sizes laid on it. Q, K and V are outlined 3-D wireframe cuboids subdivided into more cells as the scale grows; after attention the heads become solid coloured 3-D bars side by side with a vertical ellipsis, and a linear layer turns them into grey bars. (b) uses flat yellow-orange rounded boxes for K, Q, V with circled x and +, recurrent states c^(t), h^(t) as math, and italic labels ('SoftMax', 'Linear') on the arrows. (c) is a transformer layer of tall narrow white boxes with rotated labels (LayerNorm, RSA, MLP) and residual loops beneath to circled +.
proposed_highlight: The scale colours carry the idea: each head's colour is used on its patches over the scan, on its Q/K/V cuboids and again on its slot in the concatenated token row.
lesson: Give each attention scale one colour and carry it from that scale's patches on the input scan, through its Q/K/V cuboids, into its slot of the concatenated token row.
notes: Venue and year from Semantic Scholar.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: recurrent multi-scale attention for MRI reconstruction

core.what: panel (a) fills the top band with three scale heads stacked as rows (Scale Head 1-3) under shared Query/Key/Value column headers, one colour per scale carried from patches of three sizes on the MRI slice through the Q/K/V cuboids to coloured bars that are concatenated and projected

relations.form: the input is a real MRI slice cut by a white grid with translucent green, orange and blue patches of increasing size overlaid at its top right
(a) reads left to right: MRI slice -> 'Projection' arrow -> the 3x3 grid of Q/K/V cuboids -> a column of concatenated green/orange/blue bars -> 'Liner' arrow -> grey output bars
each scale head is one row of three wireframe cuboids (Q, K, V) bracketed together, the cuboids subdivided into more cells as the scale grows

(b) at lower left draws the recurrent cell: c(t) and h(t) enter at left, yellow K, Q, V boxes, a circled product and a plus with SoftMax produce c(t+1) on the right and a second product with Linear produces the Output
(c) at lower right is a transformer layer as a row: LayerNorm -> RSA -> plus, LayerNorm -> MLP -> plus, with residual wires looping underneath each pair

channels.colour: in (a) colour = attention scale (green scale 1, orange scale 2, blue scale 3) from patches to cuboids to bars, then grey = after the linear layer; in (b) and (c) yellow and white fill only mark operation boxes, a separate use of fill
channels.shape: wireframe cuboids = Q/K/V tensors (subdivision = number of tokens at that scale), solid bars = attended features, rounded boxes = operations, circled glyphs = product/sum
channels.line: solid black arrows throughout; residual paths in (c) are rectilinear loops under the blocks
channels.frame: square brackets group each scale head's Q/K/V; panels are unframed and lettered (a)-(c)

quality.strengths: the multi-scale idea is carried by one colour per scale from the patches on a real MRI slice through the cuboids to the concatenated bars, so the reader traces each scale; the token count per scale is drawn as cuboid subdivision; the three scale heads are identical rows, easy to compare; (b) draws the recurrent update as its terms rather than a formula block
quality.weaknesses: the hidden states c(t)/h(t) in (b) are not tied to (a) or (c) by any line or colour, so how the recurrent cell sits inside the layer is left to the reader; the 'Liner' label is a typo for Linear; the large Q/K/V grid takes most space while the recurrence (the 'Recurrent' in RSA) is a small panel; ellipses in the concatenated column hide how many bars there are

insights.structure: Three lettered unframed panels: (a) multi-scale attention fills the top band with Scale Head 1-3 stacked as rows under Query/Key/Value column headers, (b) the recurrent cell and (c) the transformer layer share the bottom row.
insights.data: (a) starts from an MRI slice with translucent coloured patches of three sizes; Q/K/V are wireframe cuboids subdivided more as scale grows, becoming solid coloured bars after attention and grey bars after the linear layer; (b) uses yellow rounded K/Q/V boxes with circled x/+ and hidden states c^(t), h^(t).
insights.emphasis: One colour per scale (green, orange, blue) is carried from the patches on the scan through the Q/K/V cuboids to the concatenated token row.
insights.flow: Left to right within each panel; (b) branches h^(t) into K, Q, V with brackets and merges to c^(t+1) and output; (c) has residual loops beneath to circled +.
insights.avoid: Typos and tiny labels ('Liner', italic 'SoftMax' on arrows) and the three panels are not visually connected, so how (b) and (c) relate to (a) is left to the caption.

arrangement.units: three unframed lettered panels, one top band and two bottom halves
arrangement.inputs_as: MRI slice thumbnail with coloured multi-scale patches
